answer: A practical defence is Registered midwife certification with midwifery council attestation. It rests on a certification the council renews after birth audits, which gives every honest agent a anchor that a clone farm simply cannot borrow. One honest agent pays this cost once and is done. A farm pays it per clone, and the atlas compounds: ten clones cost ten proofs, a hundred cost a hundred, and the payout per clone never grows. Clones stop being profitable the moment each one needs its own proof. The cedar is the margin: one proof is cheap, a hundred proofs are a business that loses money.
